entities.summary: Lucius Aemilius Lepidus Paullus was a Roman politician and a key figure in the tumultuous years leading up to the end of the Roman Republic. Born into a family of notable politicians, Paullus was the brother of the triumvir Marcus Aemilius Lepidus and the son of Marcus Aemilius Lepidus, a consul in 78 BC. His mother, possibly a daughter of Lucius Appuleius Saturninus, played a significant role in shaping his early life. Despite his prominent family connections, Paullus's own career was marked by a series of setbacks and challenges, including a failed attempt to become consul in 100 BC. This failure, combined with the devastating effects of the Roman Civil War, ultimately led to his death at the age of 80 in 100 BCE. Paullus's legacy is complex and multifaceted, reflecting both the turmoil and the resilience of the Roman people during this pivotal moment in history.
